title: What Is an Inference Engine, Anyway? — Charles Frye, Modal
talk_summary: Charles Frye explains the internals of LLM inference engines (SGLang/vLLM): the server/tokenizer/scheduler/model-runner process split, prefill vs decode workloads, KV caching, CUDA graphs, and speculative decoding.

takeaways.technique: Treat queuing as a failure state; scale replicas on congestion
takeaways.what_they_do: Operators watch time-to-first-token and inter-token latency; rising queue depth signals under-provisioning, and they add replicas rather than let queues grow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think of that as essentially like a failure state of the engine... I've deployed my engine improperly. If I get to the case where I have KV cache thrashing

takeaways.what_they_do: Engines split input processing (high arithmetic, parallel) from token generation (sequential, memory-bound) because they have different performance profiles and code paths.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it really feels like there's two subworkloads going on. there's the like workload to do your prefills... And then there's work to do the decodes

takeaways.technique: Prefix/KV cache reuse for shared system prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Engines cache computed prefixes so requests sharing a long system prompt reuse computation instead of recomputing it per request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: especially if you have like a giant system prompt for like an agent system that's tens of thousands of tokens... it's like quite nice to be able to share that across users

takeaways.technique: Run eval scripts against the real deployment and log token IDs
takeaways.what_they_do: Before/after deploys they hit the live endpoint with benchmark scripts, log traces and token IDs, and thread user correctness feedback back to specific requests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to hit your actual deployment with like evaluation benchmarking type scripts... log the token IDs

takeaways.technique: Log more metrics than you think you need
takeaways.what_they_do: For performance debugging they over-log metrics because unexpected cross-correlations make bugs easy to find.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the more metrics that you log uh the better like more metrics than you think you need um because you never know which crossorrelation
